headline: High: shared filesystem and broad workspace write make prompt injection, data leakage, and state corruption plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and act on filesystem content, while Cline shares workspace files and can use MCP/browser tools. That creates a plausible default bridge where attacker-controlled files or outputs from one agent can be interpreted as instructions by the other. The pathway is not proven universal, but it is not blocked by either profile.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or file tree
IF Cline ingests AutoGPT-written files as task context or instructions
IF an MCP server exposes untrusted content into either agent's prompt
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable MCP servers for the pair
Treat all inter-agent files as untrusted input
Add a manual review step before either agent reads the other's outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress; Cline reads and writes workspace files and can send content to a configured model provider and MCP servers. If sensitive files are present in the shared workspace, both agents can access them and Cline may transmit them outward. The profiles do not show PHI, so this is not critical, but the leakage path exists in default setups.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are stored in the shared workspace
IF Cline's configured model provider receives file contents
IF AutoGPT is allowed to read the same directory tree
mitigations: Move sensitive files out of the shared workspace
Restrict Cline to a non-sensitive subfolder
Disable file attachment or auto-ingest features
Review outbound prompts for secrets before execution
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries at the filesystem layer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and touch the filesystem; Cline also writes files and modifies git state, while AutoGPT has no multiple-instance support. In a shared workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide without locking, causing lost work or corrupted state. This is a default-dangerous overlap, not just an unusual configuration.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory tree
IF either agent edits git-tracked files
IF AutoGPT is run with more than one instance despite its concurrency limit
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate workspace
Pause one agent before the other writes
Avoid git operations while both are active
Use a lock file for shared resources
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level write serialization

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can take actions from workspace content and has browser/MCP/tooling, while AutoGPT can generate outputs that Cline may treat as task input. If AutoGPT produces incorrect facts or instructions, Cline can operationalize them into shell, browser, or git actions with little verification. That makes downstream mistakes likely and potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF Cline consumes AutoGPT output as authoritative task context
IF Cline is permitted to execute shell or git actions from that context
IF no human verification step is inserted between agents
mitigations: Require human review of AutoGPT outputs before Cline acts
Limit Cline to read-only mode for handoff files
Use a checklist to verify facts before execution
Keep AutoGPT outputs in a staging folder
requires-engineering: add structured validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare regulated data handling, residency, or retention commitments. The main compliance issue is operational: Cline handles model-provider API keys and can send workspace content to external services, while AutoGPT has allowlisted egress. Without a declared mismatch, the compliance risk is limited and mostly configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace
IF Cline's provider or MCP servers are outside the required jurisdiction
IF retention policies differ between the configured providers
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Select compliant providers and MCP servers
Document retention settings before use
Rotate exposed API keys if needed
requires-engineering: enforce residency and retention policy checks
